name: Colorado Watershed Restoration Grants
summary: Rolling grants in Colorado for planning, engineering and implementation of watershed work such as stream and floodplain restoration, revegetation and gully stabilisation, including post-wildfire protection projects. Non-profits and governments can apply.

eligibility.rule: Not a local government outside the National Flood Insurance Program
Applicant is neither a federal agency nor a private landowner
Capacity-building request accompanies a planning, engineering or implementation application
Involve diverse local or regional watershed interests and allow all interested watershed parties to participate
Urgent work where delay could affect life, property, water supply and other infrastructure
Commit to protecting or restoring ecological links between land and water while protecting people and property
Plan, design or project is financially and technically feasible
Implementation work and design are informed by a planning effort

co_finance.applies_to: 25% planning, engineering and capacity building; 50% implementation

documents: Evidence of matching funds, such as an award letter, where match applies

calls.label: Rolling applications from February 2026

status.quote: The CWCB will accept applications on a rolling basis starting February 13, 2026, until the available funds are obligated.

opens.quote: The CWCB will accept applications on a rolling basis starting February 13, 2026, until the available funds are obligated.

calls.note: Open until the available funds are obligated

applicant_types.quote: Governmental entities - municipalities, districts, enterprises, counties, and State of Colorado agencies. Federal agencies are encouraged to work with local entities. (Local governments that do not participate in the National Flood Insurance Program will not be eligible for funding). Colorado's Tribal Governments Private entities - mutual ditch companies, non-profit corporations, and partnerships.

access.quote: All grant applications must be submitted via the CWCB Portal

window.quote: The CWCB will accept applications on a rolling basis starting February 13, 2026, until the available funds are obligated.

effort.quote: Prior to submitting an application, interested parties must contact the CWCB to discuss potential projects.
All grant applications must be submitted via the CWCB Portal along with the current "Statement of Work" and "Budget & Schedule.
CWCB staff will determine if the required documentation has been submitted. The application will be accepted once all documentation has been received.
CWCB staff will review and score the applications. Once scored, a funding recommendation will be made to the CWCB Director.
The CWCB Director will have approval authority for funding recommendations.

eligibility.quote: (Local governments that do not participate in the National Flood Insurance Program will not be eligible for funding).
Federal agencies and private landowners are not eligible to receive grant funds
Capacity building grants must be submitted in conjunction with a planning, engineering, or implementation grant.

a commitment to collaborative approaches, involving locally and/or regionally based diverse interests within the watershed in question, with participation open to all interested parties in the watershed.
That the need for the plan or project is urgent and if delayed may result in negative impacts to life, property, water supply, and other infrastructure
a commitment to restoring or protecting the ecological processes that connect land and water while protecting lives and property
That the plan, design, or project is financially and technically feasible
That an implementation grant, including project design, has been informed through a planning effort

co_finance.quote: A minimum of 25% match is required for all Capacity Building, Planning, and Engineering Grants. A minimum of 50% match is required for all Implementation Grants. Project costs may consist of a combination of in-kind and cash match, but no more than half of the match may be in the form of in-kind services.

documents.quote: All grant applications must be submitted via the CWCB Portal along with the current "Statement of Work" and "Budget & Schedule.
Applicants should identify match as pending or secure and provide evidence of matching funds (such as an award letter).

after_award.quote: The applicant shall provide the CWCB progress reports and expenditure reports every six months, beginning from the date of the execution of a contract.
